items.title: Pay claimed import duties to release parcel
items.computation: The letter states an explicit calendar due date (09.11.2026) rather than a period to be calculated, so no statutory period computation applies. Document date is 05.11.2026 (a Thursday); the stated due date of 09.11.2026 (a Monday) is taken as printed.

warnings: This letter shows strong signs of being a parcel/customs scam ('Zoll'/import-duty phishing): the payee named for the bank transfer is a private company ('Intl. Parcel Clearing Ltd.'), not the German customs administration (Zoll/Hauptzollamt), which never collects import VAT via a private Ltd. and an ordinary IBAN transfer.

The letter insists on contact 'ausschließlich per WhatsApp' via a mobile number, which is not how German customs or licensed parcel services communicate about import duties — a typical pressure/isolation tactic used in scams.
There is a short, pressuring deadline (only a few days) combined with a threat that the parcel will be destroyed or returned, which is a classic urgency tactic used in phishing/scam letters.

The itemised table is inconsistent: the 'Einfuhrumsatzsteuer' (import VAT) row shows no amount while 'Bearbeitungsentgelt Zollabwicklung' shows 21,40 and 'Zu zahlen' shows 17,50, summing to the total of 38,90 — the missing line item suggests a sloppily assembled or fabricated invoice.

The recipient's address (Neu-Beispielstadt) does not match the sender's location (Musterstadt) and appears to be in a different postal region, which should be double-checked against any real shipment the person is actually expecting.

Recommendation: do not transfer any money and do not contact the WhatsApp number; verify independently with the actual shipping carrier (e.g. DHL, Deutsche Post, UPS) or the Zoll/Hauptzollamt using their official contact channels before taking any action.
